description: The head of corporate finance must authorize a group cash-pooling rollout and finalize the participating entities, activation date, opening sweep, operating reserve, and approval controls, with input from legal entity management, treasury operations, financial systems, and compliance.

shared_context.S1: The group has six operating entities, identified as E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, and E6, and is considering a centralized cash-pooling arrangement.
shared_context.S2: The proposed arrangement would let participating entities sweep surplus cash into a central concentration account and draw funds back for ordinary operating needs.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the rollout and set its operating conditions.
shared_context.S4: The group's normal treasury approval meeting includes a confirmation from legal entity management, treasury operations, financial systems, and compliance before the final authorization is recorded.

PF1.text: Raj confirmed in an entity-law memorandum received this morning that E4 cannot participate in the proposed cash pool because its local borrowing and security restrictions prohibit the required cross-guarantee; the memorandum has not yet been attached to the approval packet.

PF2.text: Marta's treasury review this week confirmed that exactly $1,800,000 can be swept from the participating entities on activation while $500,000 must remain outside the pool as their combined minimum operating reserve; these figures have not yet been entered in the cash-pooling worksheet.

PF3.text: Jonas confirmed with the bank-file and ERP teams this morning that the required payment-file cutover will be ready on July 1, 2026; the date is still absent from the systems implementation calendar.

PF4.text: Nadia's compliance review completed this week requires two named internal approvers to sign off before the central account is activated or any opening sweep occurs; the control has not yet been added to the treasury procedure.

acceptance_conditions: The cash-pooling rollout must be authorized.
The participating entities must be exactly E1, E2, E3, E5, and E6, excluding E4.
The activation date must be July 1, 2026.
The opening sweep must be exactly $1,800,000.
Exactly $500,000 must remain outside the pool as the operating reserve.
Two named internal approvers must be required before activation or the opening sweep.
The settlement must include a pre-activation dual-approval commitment.
The legal restriction on E4 must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'dual_approval_before_activation' and c['target'] == 'cash_pool_activation' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The shared proposal names all six entities, but PF1 changes participating_entity_ids to exactly E1, E2, E3, E5, and E6 and supplies the legal basis that must be cited for excluding E4.
Without PF2, the settlement has no basis for setting opening_sweep_usd to exactly 1800000 or outside_pool_operating_reserve_usd to exactly 500000.
Without PF3, the rollout has no confirmed systems-ready date, so activation_date would not be set to exactly 2026-07-01.
Without PF4, the approval would omit the required dual-approval control and its pre-activation commitment before the central account or opening sweep can be used.
